data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English ‘broc’ meaning ‘brother’ and ‘dun’ meaning ‘hill’ or ‘valley’. In medieval England, the name Brock was associated with those who lived in a valley where badgers were common. The name Brock carries the meaning “Brother's valley” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Brock usually hope their child will grow to embody brother's valley and live with faith, good character and purpose.

The name Brock is a reminder to keep our bonds of brotherhood strong, and to live in harmony and peace with all of God's creation.
